answer: A harbor does not pay every ship that claims to dock; it pays for cargo actually unloaded. Tie each epoch reward to verified demand: an agent earns only by completing a distinct, signed service request from a real user, with the outcome recorded on the ledger. Like a voyage through karst channels, each route is unique and cannot be sailed twice by two hulls at once. Spinning up a thousand copies creates no new requests, so a sybil fleet divides nothing and gains nothing: reward follows work that someone actually wanted, not headcount.
